record.paper_title: Current work and open problems in the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
record.original_question: If the delay function θ satisfies the vanishing-delay conditions θ(0)=0, θ(t) \le q_1 t on I for some q_1 \in (0,1), and θ \in C^d(I), but θ is not strictly increasing on I, what convergence theory holds for piecewise-polynomial collocation solutions of the Volterra functional integro-differential and integral equations considered in the paper?

evidence.quote: The convergence analysis of piecewise polynomial collocation solutions to VFIDEs (1.2) and VFIEs (1.3) with vanishing delay functions θ that satisfy (N2) and (N3) but are not strictly increasing on I remains open but is currently being studied

artifact.category_tag: collocation methods for delay Volterra equations
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $I=[0,T]$ with $T>0$, and let $\theta:I\to I$ be a vanishing delay function satisfying:
(i) $\theta(0)=0$;
(ii) there exists $q_1\in(0,1)$ such that $\theta(t)\le q_1 t$ for all $t\in I$;
(iii) $\theta\in C^d(I)$ for some integer $d\ge 1$;
but $\theta$ is NOT assumed to be strictly increasing on $I$ (so $\theta$ may have intervals of constancy or local decrease).

Consider the Volterra functional integro-differential equation (VFIDE)
$$y'(t)=a(t)y(t)+b(t)y(\theta(t))+\int_{\theta(t)}^{t} K(t,s,y(s))\,ds,\qquad t\in I,\quad y(0)=y_0,$$
and the Volterra functional integral equation (VFIE)
$$y(t)=g(t)+\int_{\theta(t)}^{t} K(t,s,y(s))\,ds,\qquad t\in I,$$
with sufficiently smooth data $a,b,g,K$.

Given a mesh $0=t_0<t_1<\dots<t_N=T$ and an integer $m\ge 1$, let $S_m^{(0)}$ (resp. $S_m^{(-1)}$) denote the space of continuous (resp. discontinuous) piecewise polynomials of degree $\le m$ on the mesh, and consider the collocation solution determined by $m$ collocation parameters $0<c_1<\dots<c_m\le 1$.

Establish a convergence theory (global convergence orders, and where possible local superconvergence at mesh points) for the piecewise-polynomial collocation solutions of the above VFIDE and VFIE under conditions (i)–(iii) but WITHOUT the assumption that $\theta$ is strictly increasing on $I$. In particular, identify appropriate mesh constructions (e.g., quasi-$\theta$-invariant meshes) under which optimal-order convergence and superconvergence results, analogous to those known in the strictly increasing case, continue to hold.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., on piecewise linear delays via quasi-θ-invariant meshes and on multiple-delay quasi-geometric meshes) addresses related cases, but a general convergence theory for piecewise-polynomial collocation when the vanishing delay θ is not strictly increasing does not appear to have been fully established in the literature. The problem appears to still be open / under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Collocation method for Volterra integro-differential equations with piecewise delays
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous framework for collocation applied to Volterra integro-differential equations with piecewise linear delays, using quasi-θ-invariant meshes with polynomial spline spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Recent papers treat special non-strictly-increasing (piecewise linear) delay cases, indicating the general non-monotone case is still being addressed.

status_evidence.title: Analysis of continuous collocation solutions for nonlinear functional equations with vanishing delays
status_evidence.snippet: Convergence analysis of collocation solutions assuming standard vanishing-delay conditions including strict monotonicity.
status_evidence.claim: Standard convergence theory presumes strictly increasing θ, leaving the non-monotone case open.
